title: Gaza’s Ceasefire Leaves Palestinians Trapped Behind a Moving Line
content:
UN rights officials warn that repeated displacement, attacks near encampments and restrictions on shelter materials are making return increasingly difficult.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 2 November 2026 (IDN) — A ceasefire may have reduced the scale of fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended the displacement of Palestinians. Nor has it given most families a realistic prospect of returning home.

The United Nations Human Rights Office, OHCHR, warned on 30 October that Israeli military operations continued to force Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip. Homes and public infrastructure were still being destroyed, displacement sites had come under attack, and families were being pushed away from areas close to the Israeli-controlled “Yellow Line”.

“The nightmare of displacement in Gaza is both acute and chronic,” said Ajith Sunghay, head of the UN Human Rights Office in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

Many Palestinians displaced before the ceasefire cannot return because their former neighbourhoods lie beyond the Yellow Line. Others have been uprooted repeatedly from places where they sought temporary shelter.

title: OPINION: In a Country That Needs Heroes, Here Are a Few Standouts This Election Season
content:
By Jeff Cohen and Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO | 2 November 2026 (IDN) — In a play by Bertolt Brecht, the persecuted astronomer Galileo says: “Unhappy the land that needs heroes.”

Right now, the United States is unhappy enough to need a lot of heroes – and during this election year, many have emerged. Here are five of the notable ones.

No other major candidate this year has been the target of so many shameless and racist smears as Abdul El-Sayed, a 41-year-old Muslim American who is one of the most articulate and persuasive campaigners to arise since Zohran Mamdani. The former health official in Michigan is in a toss-up race for the U.S. Senate against former Rep. Mike Rogers, who is a nonstop fountain of MAGA talking points and deceptive campaign messaging – reinforced by President Trump – that tries to cast El-Sayed as a terrorist “jihadist.”

title: OPINION: How to Stop the US-Israel War on Iran
content:
Arab states must reject Israeli hegemony and build a regional security framework independent of Washington.

By Jeffrey D. Sachs and Sybil Fares

NEW YORK | 31 October 2026 (IDN) — The war that Israel and the United States launched against Iran on 28 February is in a lull, not at an end. Major combat has paused, diplomacy has stalled, and both sides are preparing for the next round. To understand why the fighting will soon resume, we need to understand the motivations of the two governments that started it. Neither of them wants peace. Israel’s leadership seeks domination over the Middle East, and the United States seeks to preserve its domination over the world. Stating these aims underscores that both governments operate in a delusional world.

title: Eleven Votes, but No Clear Road to the UN’s Top Office
content:
Rebeca Grynspan widens her lead as the Security Council’s seventh straw poll leaves the decisive question of possible vetoes unanswered.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 31 October 2026 (IDN) — Rebeca Grynspan has strengthened her claim to become the next United Nations Secretary-General, winning support from 11 of the Security Council’s 15 members in its latest informal ballot. Yet the Costa Rican economist remains short of the agreement that matters most: acceptance by all five powers able to block her appointment. Türkiye’s late nomination of veteran diplomat Feridun Sinirlioğlu has now added another possible route out of the deadlock.

The seventh straw poll, held on 30 October, gave Grynspan her strongest result so far. But the Council’s return to ballots that conceal whether opposition comes from permanent or elected members has made the outcome harder to interpret. A larger majority has emerged without establishing whether a potential veto has disappeared.

title: ESSAY: The World to Come
content:
Jewish Mysticism and the Politics of Emancipation

By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 30 October  2026 (IDN) — What if the world we hope for is not somewhere in the distant future? What if, in some strange sense, it already exists? This is one possibility opened by the Zohar, the great masterpiece of Jewish mysticism.

Composed in medieval Spain and written largely as a mystical commentary on the Torah, the Zohar would seem an unlikely place to look for radical political ideas. It speaks of God, creation, the soul, good and evil, Scripture’s mysteries, and the hidden structure of reality. It is a profoundly religious work and, in many respects, a profoundly conservative one.

title: OPINION: Country Before Party: Israel’s Opposition Must Not Fail This Moment
content:
The election has opened a path away from Netanyahu’s disastrous rule. Israel’s opposition must now choose: build a Jewish-Arab governing partnership or risk surrendering the country’s future to the forces tearing it apart.

By Alon Ben-Meir*|

NEW YORK | 30 October 2026 (IDN) — Israel stands at a historic crossroads. The government that emerges from this election will determine whether the country begins to repair its democracy and recover its moral bearings—or continues toward deeper division, international isolation, and the erosion of its founding promise.

For Israel’s opposition, this is no ordinary coalition negotiation. It tests whether its leaders have the courage to put country before party, personal ambition, and ideological prejudice.

The parliamentary arithmetic offers an opening. The completed count gives parties opposed to Benjamin Netanyahu a combined 67 of the Knesset’s 120 seats: 48 for the Jewish opposition parties and 19 for the Arab-led parties. Netanyahu’s bloc holds 53. These numbers create an opportunity to replace him, not an agreement on how to govern.

title: Latecomers Crowd the Race for the Next UN Chief
content:
UAE candidate Lana Nusseibeh faces questions over Sudan as Türkiye weighs a last-minute entry by former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 29 October 2026 (IDN) — The contest to succeed António Guterres as United Nations Secretary-General should be moving toward a decision by now. Instead, it is growing more crowded—and harder to predict.

Six informal polls among Security Council members have failed to produce a candidate acceptable to all five permanent members. Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica has often led the field, but she has not escaped opposition from veto-holding countries. Nor has any other contender.

The deadlock has opened the door to latecomers.

The United Arab Emirates nominated Lana Zaki Nusseibeh on 21 October, little more than two months before Guterres leaves office. Türkiye is now considering nominating Feridun Hadi Sinirlioğlu, a former foreign minister and UN ambassador who currently heads the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE).
snippet:
UAE candidate Lana Nusseibeh faces questions over Sudan as Türkiye weighs a last-minute entry by former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu.

title: The Weight of Gold: Capitalism and the Limits of Rebellion
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 28 October 2026 (IDN) — At first glance, Padraic McKinley’s The Weight (2026), starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe, appears to be a familiar Depression-era adventure: a group of convicts, desperate for freedom, must transport a fortune in gold through the treacherous wilderness of Oregon. Dangerous river crossings, betrayals, uneasy alliances, and the ever-present possibility of death fill the journey. Yet beneath the conventions of the survival thriller lies something considerably more ambitious: a parable about capitalism, the exploitation of the vulnerable, and the terrible price exacted by a society in which wealth is valued more highly than human life.
